subject.title: fix(gateway): force exit on zombie shutdown + 503 healthz during shutdown

question: Should Gateway accept the default post-clean-shutdown process.exit(0) watchdog, the OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_POST_SHUTDOWN_EXIT_TIMEOUT_MS override, and strict internal /healthz?strict=1 503 semantics as the recovery contract for zombie shutdowns?
rationale: The code path is reviewable and proven, but the remaining choice is an operator-facing availability and compatibility tradeoff that automation should not decide.

options.title: Accept the recovery contract
options.body: Merge after Gateway-owner review accepts the forced-exit default, env override, and strict supervised probe behavior as the intended availability tradeoff.

options.title: Narrow the operator surface
options.body: Ask for a revision that removes or constrains the env timeout surface while preserving the strict probe and zombie telemetry pieces.

options.title: Pause for another design
options.body: Pause or close if maintainers prefer diagnosing handle leaks or a supervisor-only repair over process-level forced exit after clean shutdown.

recommendation.title: Accept the recovery contract
recommendation.body: Merge after Gateway-owner review accepts the forced-exit default, env override, and strict supervised probe behavior as the intended availability tradeoff.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main Gateway/CLI refactor ownership makes this the best available routing candidate for the shutdown/probe contract decision.
